Elena —

Appreciate the clear list. Below are concise, SIG-friendly answers and links to evidence. I also attached a 2-page summary and a regional failover diagram (see attachments). If you want a single-slide summary for the SIG matrix we can produce that as well.

1) RTO / RPO targets (by deployment):
- Hosted API (shared): RTO: 15 minutes for request routing failover across active regions, 1 hour for control-plane recovery; RPO: near-zero for request routing (active replication), customer data RPO depends on service (see backups).
- Redwood Dedicated (customer-dedicated GPU pools): RTO: 1–4 hours depending on configured failover policy (can be warm-standby with <1 hour); RPO: minutes to 1 hour with cross-region async replication when enabled.
- Redwood Private (VPC / on-prem): RTO/RPO are customer-controlled; we provide runbook templates and automation hooks. Default guidance: RTO: customer-defined; we recommend warm-standby patterns for <2 hour RTO.

Notes: RTO is our target for service-level recovery; customers can elect more aggressive setups (active-active or geo-replication) for tighter RTO/RPO.

2) Backups & retention (high level):
- Configuration & control-plane metadata: snapshot every 4 hours; retained 30 days (config snapshots in S3 with versioning).
- Customer content (storage/long-form artifacts): daily snapshot + continuous replication when object storage is used; retention policy is configurable per account (default 30d).
- Model binaries/weights: immutable artifacts stored in our artifact registry; objects are stored redundantly across regions with lifecycle rules (retained until deprecated).
- Ephemeral KV caches / decoding caches: not persisted long-term (designed for performance, not durability).

3) Regional failover behavior:
- Routing: smart routing layer detects region-level capacity or outage and will route new requests to healthy regions automatically within 15–45 seconds for control-plane routing changes; existing sessions may need reconnection depending on client behavior.
- Failover type: combination of automated routing + policy-driven fallback (can be configured for strict regional affinity).
- Dependencies: DNS TTL is low (30s) for hosted endpoints; traffic is proxied through our edge mesh which performs health checks. Persistent sessions that rely on in-region KV cache may observe transient degradation; we provide automatic cache warm-up heuristics for commonly used prefixes.

4) DR exercise & evidence:
- Most recent tabletop + partial failover exercise: 2026-09-10 (scope: hosted API region failover, control-plane recovery, smoke tests).
- Outcome: successful failover to secondary region; minor issue with a third-party monitoring integration that was fixed in follow-up action.
- Evidence attached: redwood_bcdr_summary.pdf (exercise report) and regional_failover_diagram.png (logical). Full runbook and test logs are available in the linked Drive folder.
